raw.thesis: Narma is an innovative venture aiming to provide an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" for AI-first companies. Its core innovation lies in creating a three-layered system to observe, understand, and automate work processes using AI. This system begins with lightweight desktop sensors (Layer 1) to capture employee work patterns, including application usage and time allocation. An "Intelligence Layer" (Layer 2) then processes this data to discern employee intent, the business value of tasks, and identify "drift" from intended workflows. Finally, an "Execution Layer" (Layer 3) acts as an "Agent Factory," automatically generating, deploying, and monitoring AI agents to capitalize on high-ROI automation opportunities, complete with approval gates. This approach is distinct because it leverages existing foundation models, rather than building new LLMs, to focus on the "Work Graph" – understanding where resources are consumed and where AI can intervene effectively. The venture aims to provide continuous AI lift by observing work, deciding AI actions, and continuously building agents. This solution is specifically for AI-first companies struggling with a lack of telemetry for AI savings, unreliable ROI measurement, and systemic drift in operations. The founder seeks to build a growth startup by addressing these critical pain points for AI-first companies looking to scale their automation efforts. Based on the description, the venture is currently at the idea stage, as it outlines the concept and vision without mentioning any built product or user engagement.
